newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power prices fall in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power prices fall in thin talk.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. ended softer Monday against Friday's levels in thin talk and mild autumn weather in the region, market sources said.
Today's forecasts indicated temperatures in most of the Southeast would peak in the 80's Fahrenheit degrees and bottom in the 50's.
Next week's outlook predicted the entire area would experience above-normal to much-above normal temperatures.

Peak, non-firm electricity during heavy load hours on Tuesday for delivery into the northern part of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) distribution system was assessed at $14.00-$15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Friday's quote of $15.00-$17.00 for Monday.
Off-peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday in northern TVA were discussed at $10.00-$12.00, lower than Friday's range of $12.00-$13.00 for Monday.
At the Georgia-Florida border, peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday was valued at $22.00-$22.50, a tighter range than Friday's $22.00-$23.00.
TVA was heard offering peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at $18.00 a MWh, compared with $15.00 and $16.00 for delivery this past Sunday and Saturday.
Florida Power Corp's 825 megawatt (MW) Crystal River 3 nuclear unit in Red Level, Fla., and Duke Power Co's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear in Seneca, S.C., remained shut, with no restart dates.
